fields.meta_title: B2B Landing Page Examples and How to Build One | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Four B2B landing page examples with the routing behind each form, and how Emergent builds a page that sends each lead to the right rep.
fields.h1: Build a B2B Landing Page That Routes Every Lead
fields.hero_description: Describe the buyer and the campaign. Emergent builds the B2B landing page, the form that qualifies each company and the rule that sends it to the right rep.
fields.features_heading: What Each B2B Page Comes With
fields.features_subheading: The page a buying committee reads, plus the qualification rules and lead records your sales team works from.
fields.feature_1:
A page written for one kind of buyer

Name the companies you sell to and the action you want from them, such as a demo or a quote. Emergent writes each section for that buyer, and you revise any part of it by prompting.
fields.feature_2:
Leads stored with the company attached

Every form submission becomes a row in a database you own, with the company's headcount and the campaign behind the visit. Export the table or sync each new lead to your CRM.
fields.feature_3:
One page per named account

Pages for named accounts read the company from the link, then show its name and a case study from its industry. Visits and form fills from that company stay on one account record.
fields.feature_4:
Routing rules written as sentences

Write the routing rule in plain words, such as headcount over 200 goes to the enterprise team. Emergent builds it into the form, and each lead lands with the owner that rule names.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts for deals already open

Once a lead matches an open deal in HubSpot or another CRM, the deal owner hears about it. A Slack message or an email to the owner names the person and the page they filled in.
fields.feature_6:
Your repository holds the code

Export the page and its lead tables to your GitHub repository at any point. Run it on Emergent under a custom domain, which uses credits, or deploy it on servers you manage.

fields.usecase_heading: Four B2B Pages and Where Their Leads Go
fields.tab_content_1:
Each target account lands on a page with its own name

Cobalt Freight picked 40 target accounts for its logistics software, and reps send each one a link to a page that greets the company by name. Every visit and form fill is saved to that account's record. When anyone from Globex Logistics fills in the form, account owner Priya Nair gets a Slack direct message.
fields.tab_content_2:
Headcount decides who answers the demo request

Ledgerline's demo form asks finance teams for company size next to their name and work email. Companies with 200 or more employees see account executive Marcus Hale's calendar and book a slot on the spot. Smaller teams receive a self-serve booking link and a recorded product tour by email.
fields.tab_content_3:
Open deals hear about every benchmark download

Finance leaders who want Fieldnote's annual procurement benchmark enter a work email to download it. Each download is checked against open deals in HubSpot. When Initech's controller downloads the report, rep Sara Lindqvist finds a note on the Initech deal.
fields.tab_content_4:
The price list goes out unless the order runs past $5,000

Distributors like Northwind Supply take wholesale account applications from cleaning contractors and facilities teams. Each application asks for expected monthly spend. Anything at $5,000 or more goes to regional rep Tom Okafor by email, while smaller accounts get the standard wholesale price list by return email.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a B2B Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Example galleries show the hero section. These steps start at the form and end with what sales sees after a company converts.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose the account or the segment
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Lead with a cost the buyer reports on
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Show proof from a peer company
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide who the page is for before writing a line. One named account can justify its own page, while a list of several hundred companies usually gets one page per industry. The narrower the audience, the more specific the headline and the proof can be.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the headline around a number the buyer already tracks, such as freight spend per shipment or days lost to month-end close. Put the product category in the subhead so a procurement lead knows what is on sale by the end of the first line.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick a case study from the visitor's industry and size band, and place its result near the form. A carrier trusts another carrier's numbers more than a wall of software logos. Name the customer and the job title of the person quoted.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Every field on the form should change where the lead goes next. Headcount can pick the team, and region can pick the rep. Anything else waits for the first call, when the buyer has a reason to answer and a person to answer to.
fields.howto_step_5_des: State the rule in plain words: 200 employees or more books with an account executive, and smaller teams get a booking link. Submit a test lead from each band and confirm both reach the right inbox before the campaign starts spending.
fields.howto_step_6_des: A buyer who is not ready for a demo may still want the pricing sheet or a recorded walkthrough. Put that option below the main form. A visit that stops short of a meeting still ends with a name in your lead table.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Save the campaign and the page with every lead, then count how many became qualified opportunities 30 days later. A page with fewer form fills that books meetings with the right accounts beats one that collects students and competitors.

plan.angle: The top 10 is example roundups (Unbounce, ConvertFlow, Yarnit, Landingmetrics), design galleries (Dribbble, Behance), a Reddit thread and best-practice posts (Instapage, Directive, Heyflow). They show heroes and list tips but stop at the form. This page defines the term up top for the AI Overview, then walks through four B2B pages with the routing behind the form (an ABM page per target account, demo requests routed by headcount, a gated report that updates the open deal, a wholesale account application), and answers the PAA questions plainly, cost questions included.
tab_stories: Cobalt Freight, logistics software, runs a LinkedIn ABM campaign to 40 named accounts, each sent to its own page that shows the account's name, and when anyone from Globex Logistics fills in the form, account owner Priya Nair gets a Slack direct message.

Ledgerline, accounting software for finance teams, asks for headcount on its demo request form, and companies with 200 or more employees go straight to account executive Marcus Hale's calendar while smaller ones get a self-serve booking link.

Fieldnote, a procurement software company, gates its annual spend benchmark behind a work email form, and when a download comes from a company with an open deal in HubSpot, a note lands on that deal for the rep.

Northwind Supply, a janitorial distributor, takes wholesale account applications, and any business expecting to order $5,000 or more a month goes to regional rep Tom Okafor while the rest receive the standard price list.

claims_to_source: B2B (business-to-business) means a company selling products or services to other businesses rather than to consumers
Account-based marketing (ABM) targets a defined list of named accounts with personalized campaigns instead of a broad audience
LinkedIn Campaign Manager lets advertisers target ads to a list of named companies they upload, and a company list needs at least 300 companies
The four types of B2B markets are commonly listed as producers, resellers, governments and institutions
Amazon Business is Amazon's marketplace for business buyers, so Amazon sells B2B as well as to consumers
HubSpot's API can create a note and associate it with a deal
A landing page is a standalone page built for one campaign or goal, with a single call to action
